lessons.content_md:
# The Gym vs. The Real World 🏋️‍♂️

Running an AI system is broken down into two completely different phases: **Training** and **Inference**.

## 1. Training (The Gym)

Imagine a boxer preparing for a championship fight. They spend months in the gym lifting weights, running miles, and sparring. It takes massive amounts of energy, sweat, and time to build those muscles.

In AI, this is **Training**. 
We lock the AI in a massive data center and force it to analyze millions of examples over and over again until it learns the patterns. 
Training can take weeks or months and costs millions of dollars in electricity and supercomputer time!

## 2. Inference (The Real World)

The boxer steps out of the gym and into the real world. If someone drops a glass, the boxer's reflexes instantly catch it before it hits the floor. It took zero effort because the muscle memory was already built.

In AI, this is **Inference**. 
The model is fully trained. Now, we put it on a smartphone or a website. When a user asks it a question, the AI uses its "muscle memory" to instantly provide an answer in milliseconds. Inference requires very little computing power compared to Training.

<flipcard front="🏋️‍♂️ What is the difference between Training and Inference?" back="Training is the expensive, slow process of teaching the AI (the gym). Inference is the cheap, lightning-fast process of using the trained AI in the real world."></flipcard>
